mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within 3 months indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% over 3 months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over 3 months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances following the signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) decreases by more than 0.5% over 3 months, it signals a positive demand environment with controlled inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and CPIAUCSL decrease > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of HOUST increase and CPIAUCSL decrease on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% over 3 months, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 2% in 3 months
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over 6 months signals a strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances following the signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
